web_evidence.title: Daisy Jones & The Six — Penguin Books sample
web_evidence.note: The authorized 43-page sample contains the compiler’s author note defining the work as an oral history assembled from interviews and documents, followed by sustained, speaker-labeled first-person testimony from Daisy and other participants.

web_evidence.title: An interview with Taylor Jenkins Reid
web_evidence.note: Reid describes the entire novel as an oral history and as-told-to autobiography, explicitly says she wrote male characters in first person, and explains that the characters themselves supply all narrative information.

web_evidence.title: Taylor Jenkins Reid Explores Sex, Drugs, and Rock and Roll
web_evidence.note: In this author interview, Reid says the book has no separate traditional narrator because readers hear everything from the characters themselves in oral-history form.

web_evidence.title: Malibu Rising by Taylor Jenkins Reid book review
web_evidence.note: The Standard explicitly contrasts the author’s novels by identifying Daisy Jones & The Six as an oral history with multiple first-person narrators.

person_note: The novel’s base narrative is a fictional oral history: multiple band members, relatives, and associates provide constitutive first-person interview testimony, while an in-universe compiler frames and edits their accounts. Multiple narrators remain FIRST because they use the same narrative person. Universal “you” passages are advice or direct address, not a second-person narrative strand; song lyrics and clearly local confrontational speech are embedded material. The authorized opening, two author interviews describing the whole-book method, an explicit reputable description of multiple first-person narrators, and numerous diagnostic quotations agree. The only minor uncertainty is whether a few isolated dialogue-bucket excerpts preserve interview testimony or embedded speech, but that does not affect the book-level classification.
